newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds need US help to kick on rally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds need US help to kick on rally.

text.p: Long-dated Australian bond yields fell to their lowest level since February 1994, taking the lead from a robust U.S. market, but are seen needing their dollar bloc partner to rally further.

Traders said the market saw active two way trading after yields broke last week's post-rate cut lows, but with no major local data due out this week, the trend will be dependent on the U.S. trend amid a host of indicatiors.
"What you saw were people having to get back into the market for cover against those looking to take profits. The short-end, meanwhile, is back flat against the cash rate," one trader said.

Three-year bond yields were a tad below the official 6.50 percent cash rate, and although a further softening in monetary policy is seen possible, the market is seen needing some key data to suggest such a move is on, traders said.

The long-end, however, chased the fall in U.S. yields as the market there anticipates benign readings in a series of indicators over the next couple days, starting with the October PPI later today, which is seen rising 0.2 percent. The FOMC also meets today, but no change in policy is expected.
Meanwhile, the Westpac consumer sentiment index jumped 8.3 percent in November following last week monetary policy easing.

The local yield curve flattened as the long end outperformed, while the market generally maintained this week's tightening trend against other dollar bloc bonds. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread eased to its lowest level since late October.

The December 10-year bond futures contract hit a new 32-month high of 92.920 after the previous 92.830 peak was broken in SYCOM trading, and will be now looking to test the psychological 93.000 level, or around 7.0 percent on the physical bond yield. -- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
